_comment: Carry destination for R9-EG-A4 (#1774, whether delta-S becomes a required check), from R9-EG-B1 (#1736, the per-solve record).
The round-1 fix review of #1887 (comment 5977790144) measured the instrument finding; this file is the in-tree destination the
review named. The roster for EG-A4 is on handoff/audit-r9-fixplan, not on main. While the two disagree the newer one is right:

carries.from: the round-1 fix review of the R9-EG-B1 pull request (#1887, comment 5977790144), which planted a hub write after _refresh_model_corrections()
carries.control: Plant: one write into a hub added immediately after the _refresh_model_corrections() call in _update_current_state leaves both hub_solve_writes (tools/audit/archscore/metrics/hub_solve_writes.py, roots async_run_optimization and async_simulate) and tests/arch_score_head.py's planted-write control unmoved (ALL 7 ... PASSED at the EG-B1 round-1 head). Widening the same engine's roots to the whole scheduled cycle (_async_update_data + async_run_optimization + async_simulate) is what saw it: 71 -> 38 sites, 55 -> 28 fields across that boundary at the round-1 base/head.
carries.remeasure: Do not trust the figures: re-run the widened engine at your own merge base, and re-plant the write before deciding the metric sees it.
carries.brief: The score's hub_solve_writes and the barrier that reads it cannot see a solve-input write moved into the pre-solve state refresh: _refresh_model_corrections runs in _update_current_state, one call before the solve, outside both roots. EG-B1 relocated 5 correction fields there (solar_aperture_scale, internal_gains_profile, dhw_inlet_current, flow_curve_bias, flow_curve_indoor_target), disclosed and argued, and about 7.7 of its +20.59 dS comes from those 5 sites -- so a required delta-S can be fed by writes the solve-path barrier is blind to. The decision on making delta-S required must either widen the metric's roots to the scheduled cycle or state the blind spot; and SOLVE_PATH_HUB_WRITERS' table can be evaded the same way, so the #1736 barrier's next editor widens roots rather than trusting the table's completeness.
